aws.title: Reference: TLS-only S3 document bucket
aws.description: A versioned S3 bucket with all four public access blocks, SSE-S3 encryption, and an explicit deny for non-TLS requests. Identity permissions are prerequisites; this example does not create a private VPC endpoint or a customer-managed KMS key.

aws.opa_policy:
package reference.aws
import rego.v1

# Input: terraform show -json tfplan. Partial baseline check; not a full audit.
default allow := false
allow if {
  resources := [r | some r in input.resource_changes; r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block"; r.change.after != null]
  count(resources) > 0
  every r in resources {
    r.change.after.block_public_acls == true
    r.change.after.block_public_policy == true
    r.change.after.ignore_public_acls == true
    r.change.after.restrict_public_buckets == true
  }
}
aws.remediation: All four public-access flags true; versioning Enabled; encryption AES256. Upload a test object with an authorized identity, then confirm anonymous and signed HTTP access are denied. Deletion requires an empty bucket, including versions.

reference.prerequisites: Terraform 1.5+, AWS CLI credentials and permissions to create S3 buckets and policies. Supply a globally unique bucket_name. Grant the test identity s3:GetObject/s3:PutObject separately. AWS service principals are excluded from the transport deny to avoid redacted network-context failures.
reference.commands:
terraform init
terraform fmt -check
terraform validate
terraform plan -var="bucket_name=YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET" -out=tfplan
terraform show -json tfplan > tfplan.json
opa eval --data policy.rego --input tfplan.json "data.reference.aws.allow"
# After reviewing the plan:
terraform apply tfplan
aws s3api get-public-access-block --bucket YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET
aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET
aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET
# Teardown after removing all object versions and delete markers:
terraform destroy -var="bucket_name=YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET"
reference.expected: All four public-access flags true; versioning Enabled; encryption AES256. Upload a test object with an authorized identity, then confirm anonymous and signed HTTP access are denied. Deletion requires an empty bucket, including versions.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
: "${BUCKET_NAME:?Set BUCKET_NAME to an existing test bucket}"
aws s3api get-public-access-block --bucket "$BUCKET_NAME"
aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket "$BUCKET_NAME"
developer_guide.scope: A versioned S3 bucket with all four public access blocks, SSE-S3 encryption, and an explicit deny for non-TLS requests. Identity permissions are prerequisites; this example does not create a private VPC endpoint or a customer-managed KMS key. Terraform 1.5+, AWS CLI credentials and permissions to create S3 buckets and policies. Supply a globally unique bucket_name. Grant the test identity s3:GetObject/s3:PutObject separately. AWS service principals are excluded from the transport deny to avoid redacted network-context failures.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

azure.title: Reference: Azure storage with public networking disabled
azure.description: Deploys a StorageV2 account with TLS 1.2, HTTPS-only access, Shared Key disabled, and public network access disabled. This is a locked-down baseline: blob data remains unreachable until you separately configure a private endpoint, DNS, network connectivity, and a data-plane RBAC role.

azure.opa_policy:
package reference.azure
import rego.v1

# Input: terraform show -json tfplan. Partial baseline check; not a full audit.
default allow := false
allow if {
  resources := [r | some r in input.resource_changes; r.type == "azurerm_storage_account"; r.change.after != null]
  count(resources) > 0
  every r in resources {
    r.change.after.public_network_access_enabled == false
    r.change.after.shared_access_key_enabled == false
    r.change.after.allow_nested_items_to_be_public == false
    r.change.after.https_traffic_only_enabled == true
    r.change.after.min_tls_version == "TLS1_2"
  }
}
azure.remediation: publicNetworkAccess Disabled, allowSharedKeyAccess false, minimumTlsVersion TLS1_2. Management-plane access remains available; this does not prove private blob access works. Add and test private connectivity before storing application data.

reference.prerequisites: Terraform 1.5+, Azure CLI login, an existing subscription, and resource creation permissions. Supply subscription_id and a globally unique 3-24 character lowercase alphanumeric storage_name. Register Microsoft.Storage first if your identity cannot register providers. LRS is local redundancy, not zone or region disaster recovery.
reference.commands:
az login
terraform init
terraform fmt -check
terraform validate
terraform plan -var="subscription_id=YOUR_SUBSCRIPTION" -var="storage_name=YOURUNIQUENAME" -out=tfplan
terraform show -json tfplan > tfplan.json
opa eval --data policy.rego --input tfplan.json "data.reference.azure.allow"
# After reviewing the plan:
terraform apply tfplan
az storage account show --ids "$(terraform output -raw storage_account_id)" --query "{publicNetworkAccess:publicNetworkAccess,allowSharedKeyAccess:allowSharedKeyAccess,minimumTlsVersion:minimumTlsVersion}"
terraform destroy -var="subscription_id=YOUR_SUBSCRIPTION" -var="storage_name=YOURUNIQUENAME"
reference.expected: publicNetworkAccess Disabled, allowSharedKeyAccess false, minimumTlsVersion TLS1_2. Management-plane access remains available; this does not prove private blob access works. Add and test private connectivity before storing application data.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
az account show --output table
: "${RESOURCE_GROUP:?Set RESOURCE_GROUP to your test resource group}"
az resource list --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Deploys a StorageV2 account with TLS 1.2, HTTPS-only access, Shared Key disabled, and public network access disabled. This is a locked-down baseline: blob data remains unreachable until you separately configure a private endpoint, DNS, network connectivity, and a data-plane RBAC role. Terraform 1.5+, Azure CLI login, an existing subscription, and resource creation permissions. Supply subscription_id and a globally unique 3-24 character lowercase alphanumeric storage_name. Register Microsoft.Storage first if your identity cannot register providers. LRS is local redundancy, not zone or region disaster recovery.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

gcp.title: Reference: IAM-only Cloud Storage bucket
gcp.description: Creates a versioned Cloud Storage bucket with uniform bucket-level access and enforced public access prevention. Existing IAM grants control authenticated requests. Public access prevention does not provide a private endpoint or VPC Service Controls perimeter, and versioning is not retention lock.

gcp.remediation: publicAccessPrevention enforced, uniformBucketLevelAccess enabled, and versioning enabled in the bucket description. Anonymous access fails; authenticated object access requires an appropriate IAM role. Review inherited project roles when testing least privilege.

reference.prerequisites: Terraform 1.5+, gcloud application-default login, an existing project with Cloud Storage available, and storage bucket administration permissions. Supply project_id and a globally unique bucket_name. Bind workload IAM separately. Noncurrent object versions incur storage usage.
reference.commands:
gcloud auth application-default login
terraform init
terraform fmt -check
terraform validate
terraform plan -var="project_id=YOUR_PROJECT" -var="bucket_name=YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET" -out=tfplan
terraform show -json tfplan > tfplan.json
opa eval --data policy.rego --input tfplan.json "data.reference.gcp.allow"
# After reviewing the plan:
terraform apply tfplan
gcloud storage buckets describe gs://YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET --format=json
# After removing all object generations:
terraform destroy -var="project_id=YOUR_PROJECT" -var="bucket_name=YOUR_UNIQUE_BUCKET"
reference.expected: publicAccessPrevention enforced, uniformBucketLevelAccess enabled, and versioning enabled in the bucket description. Anonymous access fails; authenticated object access requires an appropriate IAM role. Review inherited project roles when testing least privilege.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
gcloud config get-value project
: "${PROJECT_ID:?Set PROJECT_ID to your test project}"
gcloud logging read 'severity>=ERROR' --project="$PROJECT_ID" --limit=10 --format=json
developer_guide.scope: Creates a versioned Cloud Storage bucket with uniform bucket-level access and enforced public access prevention. Existing IAM grants control authenticated requests. Public access prevention does not provide a private endpoint or VPC Service Controls perimeter, and versioning is not retention lock. Terraform 1.5+, gcloud application-default login, an existing project with Cloud Storage available, and storage bucket administration permissions. Supply project_id and a globally unique bucket_name. Bind workload IAM separately. Noncurrent object versions incur storage usage.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

kspm.title: Reference: restricted web workload with default-deny networking
kspm.description: Two non-root web replicas behind a ClusterIP Service. Default-deny networking has explicit egress permission to web pods and ingress permission from same-namespace pods labeled role=client on TCP 8080. NetworkPolicy is enforcement configuration, not a hop between the Service and Pods.

kspm.opa_policy:
package reference.kspm
import rego.v1
# Input: a single Deployment JSON, not a List or a multi-document YAML stream.
default allow := false
allow if {
  input.kind == "Deployment"
  input.spec.template.spec.automountServiceAccountToken == false
  input.spec.template.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == true
  input.spec.template.spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type == "RuntimeDefault"
  count(input.spec.template.spec.containers) > 0
  every c in input.spec.template.spec.containers {
    c.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == false
    c.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem == true
    "ALL" in c.securityContext.capabilities.drop
  }
}
kspm.manifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: csc-reference
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: csc-reference
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: web}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: web}
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 101
        runAsGroup: 101
        fsGroup: 101
        seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.28-alpine
          ports: [{containerPort: 8080}]
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi}
            limits: {cpu: 250m, memory: 128Mi}
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /, port: 8080}
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /, port: 8080}
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}
      volumes:
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {sizeLimit: 64Mi}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: csc-reference
spec:
  selector: {app: web}
  ports: [{port: 80, targetPort: 8080}]
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: csc-reference
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-client
  namespace: csc-reference
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app: web}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
    - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: {role: client}
      ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 8080}]
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-web-egress
  namespace: csc-reference
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app: web}
      ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 8080}]
kspm.remediation: Deployment available replicas = 2; allowed client receives the nginx page. An unlabeled client times out despite matching egress permission, demonstrating ingress isolation. If both succeed, verify CNI policy enforcement; port-forward is not a valid NetworkPolicy test. Egress is limited to same-namespace web pods on TCP 8080; DNS remains blocked. Replies to allowed ingress remain permitted.

reference.prerequisites: An existing Kubernetes cluster, kubectl context, and a NetworkPolicy-capable CNI. Namespace creation requires suitable RBAC. Use a Linux node. The image tag is a runnable example; pin a verified digest before production. No external ingress, TLS termination, or cross-zone scheduling is created. NetworkPolicy does not authenticate application users.
reference.commands:
kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f workload.yaml
# After review:
kubectl apply -f workload.yaml
kubectl -n csc-reference rollout status deployment/web --timeout=120s
kubectl -n csc-reference get networkpolicy
# Allowed: same namespace and matching label, numeric Service IP avoids DNS egress
WEB_IP=$(kubectl -n csc-reference get svc web -o jsonpath="{.spec.clusterIP}")
kubectl -n csc-reference run allowed --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.37 --labels=role=client --overrides='{"spec":{"securityContext":{"runAsNonRoot":true,"runAsUser":1000,"seccompProfile":{"type":"RuntimeDefault"}},"containers":[{"name":"allowed","image":"busybox:1.37","command":["wget","-T","5","-qO-","http://'"$WEB_IP"'"],"securityContext":{"allowPrivilegeEscalation":false,"capabilities":{"drop":["ALL"]}}}]}}'
kubectl -n csc-reference logs allowed
# Repeat with name denied and without the role=client label: expect a timeout.
# Remove the disposable example namespace after testing:
kubectl delete namespace csc-reference
reference.expected: Deployment available replicas = 2; allowed client receives the nginx page. An unlabeled client times out despite matching egress permission, demonstrating ingress isolation. If both succeed, verify CNI policy enforcement; port-forward is not a valid NetworkPolicy test. Egress is limited to same-namespace web pods on TCP 8080; DNS remains blocked. Replies to allowed ingress remain permitted.

developer_guide.name: Pod-to-Pod connectivity with CNI enforcement
developer_guide.contract: Namespace and Pod selectors, direction, protocol and destination port
dependencies: Client and server Pods with controlled labels
steps: Apply default-deny rules in the test namespace.
Add the required destination ingress and source egress allows.
Test the real Pod network path rather than kubectl port-forward.
tests: Confirm the matching client succeeds and an untrusted client fails.
Test DNS egress separately if the application resolves hostnames.
failures: Both clients connect: verify the CNI enforces NetworkPolicy.
Both clients fail: inspect both ingress and egress selectors and ports.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
kubectl config current-context
: "${NAMESPACE:?Set NAMESPACE to your test namespace}"
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get pods,services,endpointslices
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
developer_guide.scope: Two non-root web replicas behind a ClusterIP Service. Default-deny networking has explicit egress permission to web pods and ingress permission from same-namespace pods labeled role=client on TCP 8080. NetworkPolicy is enforcement configuration, not a hop between the Service and Pods. An existing Kubernetes cluster, kubectl context, and a NetworkPolicy-capable CNI. Namespace creation requires suitable RBAC. Use a Linux node. The image tag is a runnable example; pin a verified digest before production. No external ingress, TLS termination, or cross-zone scheduling is created. NetworkPolicy does not authenticate application users.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

cnapp.title: Reference: CNAPP Defense & MITRE ATT&CK Auto-Remediation with OPA
cnapp.description: A multi-tier CNAPP defense-in-depth architecture mapping MITRE ATT&CK techniques across perimeter WAF, KSPM admission controls, CNI microsegmentation, GuardDuty runtime detection, and EventBridge Lambda auto-containment.

cnapp.opa_policy:
package reference.kspm

import rego.v1

# CloudSecCorner Reference Architecture - Kubernetes Security Posture Management (KSPM)
# Validates Kubernetes Deployment specs against CIS Benchmarks and MITRE ATT&CK mitigation requirements.
#
# Mitigates:
# - MITRE T1078 / T1552: Disables automatic service account token mounting
# - MITRE T1068: Disables privilege escalation
# - MITRE T1611: Restricts Linux capabilities (drops ALL) and enforces runtime seccomp
# - MITRE T1059: Enforces read-only root filesystem to prevent downloading malware payloads

default allow := false

# Allow deployment only if all zero-trust container security constraints pass
allow if {
    input.kind == "Deployment"
    input.spec.template.spec.automountServiceAccountToken == false
    input.spec.template.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == true
    input.spec.template.spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type == "RuntimeDefault"
    count(input.spec.template.spec.containers) > 0
    every c in input.spec.template.spec.containers {
        c.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == false
        c.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem == true
        "ALL" in c.securityContext.capabilities.drop
    }
}

# Detailed violation reporting for Gatekeeper / Conftest
deny contains msg if {
    input.kind == "Deployment"
    input.spec.template.spec.automountServiceAccountToken != false
    msg := "KSPM-001: automountServiceAccountToken must be explicitly false (prevents token exfiltration T1552)"
}

deny contains msg if {
    input.kind == "Deployment"
    not input.spec.template.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
    msg := "KSPM-002: spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot must be true (prevents root compromise T1068)"
}

deny contains msg if {
    input.kind == "Deployment"
    input.spec.template.spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type != "RuntimeDefault"
    msg := "KSPM-003: seccompProfile.type must be RuntimeDefault (restricts syscall surface T1611)"
}

deny contains msg if {
    input.kind == "Deployment"
    some c in input.spec.template.spec.containers
    c.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
    msg := sprintf("KSPM-004: Container '%v' must have readOnlyRootFilesystem enabled", [c.name])
}

deny contains msg if {
    input.kind == "Deployment"
    some c in input.spec.template.spec.containers
    not "ALL" in c.securityContext.capabilities.drop
    msg := sprintf("KSPM-005: Container '%v' must drop ALL capabilities", [c.name])
}
cnapp.manifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cloudseccorner-production
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: workload-app
  namespace: cloudseccorner-production
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: workload-app
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: cnapp-architecture
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: workload-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: workload-app
    spec:
      # KSPM Rule 1: Prevent automatic token projection (mitigates MITRE T1078 / T1552)
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        # KSPM Rule 2: Enforce non-root execution (mitigates MITRE T1068)
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        runAsGroup: 10001
        fsGroup: 10001
        # KSPM Rule 3: Restrict system calls via runtime default seccomp profile
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: cgr.dev/chainguard/nginx:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          securityContext:
            # KSPM Rule 4: Disable privilege escalation
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            # KSPM Rule 5: Read-only root filesystem prevents dropping implants (MITRE T1059)
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            # KSPM Rule 6: Drop all Linux capabilities
            capabilities:
              drop:
                - ALL
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp-volume
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: tmp-volume
          emptyDir:
            sizeLimit: 64Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: workload-app
  namespace: cloudseccorner-production
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: workload-app
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
---
# CNI Microsegmentation: Default Deny All Ingress and Egress
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-all
  namespace: cloudseccorner-production
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
    - Egress
---
# CNI Microsegmentation: Ingress only allowed from Ingress Controller / ALB
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-ingress-from-alb
  namespace: cloudseccorner-production
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: workload-app
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
  ingress:
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: ingress-controller
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
---
# CNI Microsegmentation: Egress strictly whitelisted to internal AWS Secrets & DB
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-app-egress-controlled
  namespace: cloudseccorner-production
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: workload-app
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    # Allow DNS resolution
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector: {}
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              k8s-app: kube-dns
      ports:
        - protocol: UDP
          port: 53
cnapp.remediation: Admission webhook validates pod non-root status; CNI blocks unauthorized egress; GuardDuty flags anomalous API behavior; Lambda updates quarantine NetworkPolicy.

reference.prerequisites: Kubernetes 1.28+, OPA Gatekeeper, AWS CLI with SecurityHub, GuardDuty, and EventBridge permissions. NetworkPolicy capable CNI (Amazon VPC CNI with NetworkPolicy support or Cilium).
reference.commands:
kubectl apply -f workload.yaml
opa eval --data policy.rego --input workload.yaml "data.reference.kspm.allow"
aws guardduty get-detector
aws events list-rules --name-prefix csc-cnapp
reference.expected: Admission webhook validates pod non-root status; CNI blocks unauthorized egress; GuardDuty flags anomalous API behavior; Lambda updates quarantine NetworkPolicy.

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: A multi-tier CNAPP defense-in-depth architecture mapping MITRE ATT&CK techniques across perimeter WAF, KSPM admission controls, CNI microsegmentation, GuardDuty runtime detection, and EventBridge Lambda auto-containment. Kubernetes 1.28+, OPA Gatekeeper, AWS CLI with SecurityHub, GuardDuty, and EventBridge permissions. NetworkPolicy capable CNI (Amazon VPC CNI with NetworkPolicy support or Cilium).

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

vultr.title: Reference: S3-compatible Vultr Object Storage with private ACL & TLS
vultr.description: Deploys a Vultr Object Storage subscription with TLS transport, private access permissions, and automated lifecycle rules. Data access requires valid S3 API keys; anonymous public access is completely restricted.

reference.commands:
vultr-cli account info
terraform init
terraform plan -out=tfplan
terraform show -json tfplan > tfplan.json
opa eval --data policy.rego --input tfplan.json "data.reference.vultr.allow"
reference.expected: Vultr Object Storage provisioned with private access. Anonymous requests fail with 403 Forbidden; authenticated S3 API calls succeed.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
vultr-cli account info
: "${SUB_ID:?Set SUB_ID to an active Vultr subscription ID}"
vultr-cli instance list
developer_guide.scope: Deploys a Vultr Object Storage subscription with TLS transport, private access permissions, and automated lifecycle rules. Data access requires valid S3 API keys; anonymous public access is completely restricted. Terraform 1.5+, Vultr API key with storage permissions. Supply label for resource identification.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

oracle.title: Reference: Encrypted OCI Object Storage bucket with public access disabled
oracle.description: Deploys an OCI Object Storage bucket with NoPublicAccess, customer-managed KMS encryption, and object versioning enabled. Workload access is restricted to authenticated IAM principals.

reference.prerequisites: Terraform 1.5+, OCI CLI configured with tenancy and user credentials. Supply compartment_ocid and bucket_name.
reference.commands:
oci iam user get
terraform init
terraform plan -var="compartment_ocid=YOUR_COMPARTMENT_OCID" -out=tfplan
terraform show -json tfplan > tfplan.json
opa eval --data policy.rego --input tfplan.json "data.reference.oracle.allow"
reference.expected: OCI Object Storage bucket provisioned with access_type NoPublicAccess and versioning Enabled.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

developer_guide.scope: Deploys an OCI Object Storage bucket with NoPublicAccess, customer-managed KMS encryption, and object versioning enabled. Workload access is restricted to authenticated IAM principals. Terraform 1.5+, OCI CLI configured with tenancy and user credentials. Supply compartment_ocid and bucket_name.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.
